What the export to Jellyfin left behind

Ferrofin's own tables, removed from the exported database (what each held, and where it went):
  FerrofinIntroSkipperSegments (3 rows): Intro Skipper's segments as detected and edited; those it published stay in Jellyfin's MediaSegments.
  FerrofinMeta (1 row): Ferrofin's settings for this database and the one-time repairs it ran; nothing Jellyfin needs.
  FerrofinNew (0 rows): a table of Ferrofin's own.
  _sqlx_migrations (52 rows): Ferrofin's own migration history; nothing Jellyfin needs.
  2 indexes of Ferrofin's own on Jellyfin's tables (an index holds no data of its own).

What Jellyfin will change on its first start, running the code migrations its history leaves out (the database was adopted as Jellyfin 10.11.8):
  DisableLegacyAuthorization: turns EnableLegacyAuthorization off in system.xml, so clients that sign in the legacy way stop working until it is turned on again.
  MergeDuplicatePeople: merges people whose names differ only by case into one and deletes the others, with their metadata folders.
    Here: 1 person and 3 credits differ from others only by case.
  HarmonizeConflictingUserData: where one item has several play-state rows for a user that disagree, gives them all the most recently played one's values.
    Here: 1 play state disagrees with another of its user and item.
  UpdateNormalizedUsername: recomputes stored values from the same inputs; nothing should change.
  Before them Jellyfin copies the database (41.2 MiB) into data/SQLiteBackups, and after them it rebuilds it, so the output's volume needs about 82.4 MiB free besides the export. A start whose migrations fail restores the database from that copy and keeps the copy, one more each time.

What Jellyfin does not run, as Ferrofin already did it (its history marks it done):
  MigrateRatingLevels: Ferrofin ran its own port of it when it adopted the database, and its scans gave each season and episode the rating it inherits from its series since; run again, it would take that rating away, so that lists show them to the accounts it hides them from until Jellyfin's next scan.
  MigrateLinkedChildren: Ferrofin moved the playlist, collection and version links out of the items' data when it adopted the database; run again, it would read them again, merging back the versions split since (and stopping Jellyfin's start when another version took the place of the one split off), and delete the additional parts of every movie in parts.
  FixIncorrectOwnerIdRelationships: Ferrofin repaired the items' owners when it adopted the database; run again, it would take its owner from each additional part of a movie in parts, which would then list as a video of its own until Jellyfin's next scan.
    Here: 2 items repeat another's path, which it would delete.

Settings Jellyfin is not given:
  CertificatePath in config/network.xml: a path in Ferrofin's filesystem.
  Settings given to Ferrofin in config.toml, FERROFIN_* environment variables or command-line flags are not exported, but for the MusicBrainz server and the Studio Images repository, which outrank those plugins' own settings and are written into them.

Live TV:
  Written for Jellyfin: 2 tuners and 1 guide provider in config/livetv.xml, 3 timers (1 completed recording among them) in data/livetv/timers.json, 1 series timer in data/livetv/seriestimers.json.
  Kept in the database: 2 channels and 8 guide programmes, which Jellyfin reads as its own, with the users' data on them (1 favourite channel). Jellyfin's guide refresh updates them in place where it derives the same ids, which was checked for an M3U tuner with an XMLTV guide; for an HDHomeRun tuner or a Schedules Direct guide it was not, and a channel or programme whose id Jellyfin derives differently is replaced at the refresh, its favourites and the timers on it with it.
  Before Jellyfin's first guide refresh (its schedule runs one an hour after its start at the earliest; run Refresh Guide in its scheduled tasks to have it at once), make sure every tuner answers from inside Jellyfin's container: a refresh that cannot read a tuner's channels deletes them, with their favourites, their guide and every timer on them, as Jellyfin does on any refresh. A guide it cannot read leaves the channels, the guide and the timers as they are.
  2 timers and 1 series timer that Jellyfin kept before adoption and Ferrofin does not hold are replaced by Ferrofin's.
  MovieRecordingPath: /mnt/films is outside the data directory, so it is written as it is: Jellyfin's container must reach it at that path.
  Tuner Attic: its playlist /srv/ferrofin/tuner.m3u is a file, written as it is because every channel's id is derived from it: make it readable at that path in Jellyfin's container, or Jellyfin's guide refresh finds no channels and deletes them.
  Tuner Lounge: it is at http://127.0.0.1:5004, a loopback address, which inside Jellyfin's container is the container itself: written as it is because every channel's id is derived from it, so give the container that address (host networking), or Jellyfin's guide refresh finds no channels and deletes them.
  Not written, as their stored settings could not be read: a timer.

Plugins:
  Settings written for Jellyfin in plugins/configurations: TMDb, LDAP-Auth, Intro Skipper.
  Not part of Jellyfin, so read only once installed from its plugin catalogue: LDAP-Auth, Intro Skipper.
  LDAP-Auth: 2 links from directory uids to users in its settings; until the plugin is installed, the users who sign in through it cannot sign in.
  LDAP-Auth's LdapRootCaPath names a file on Ferrofin's server, written as it is: Jellyfin's container must reach it at that path.
  Kept as Jellyfin left them before adoption, as Ferrofin never held settings for them: the settings of Merge Versions.
  No Jellyfin counterpart, so their settings are not carried: Single Sign-On, a WASM plugin (5f0e8d1c-0000-4000-8000-000000000001).

Files and stored paths:
  cache: left out of the copy; the server's cache, log or web client, which Jellyfin does not read.
  metadata: left out of the copy; not the directory the server's settings name for it.
  The metadata directory the server's settings name was not found where the export ran, so the output's metadata holds none of it: every image and folder Jellyfin looks for there through %MetadataPath% is missing. Export again where that directory is reachable at the path the settings give.
  The database's root and library rows name another data directory than the one exported: the server ran at another path, or the directory moved since. The stored paths under it were rewritten for Jellyfin too; the export printed both directories.
  playlist.xml of 2 playlists in data/playlists, collection.xml of 1 collection in data/collections: left out of the copy. Each may hold what Jellyfin last wrote rather than the changes made in Ferrofin since (a share or a member removed, a rename), which Jellyfin's metadata refresh would merge back; Jellyfin finds the playlists and collections without them, and writes each file again from the database when it next saves the playlist or collection.
  data/collections/Odd/collection.xml: kept, though it may hold what Jellyfin last wrote rather than the changes made in Ferrofin since: its folder's name lacks [boxset], so the file is what makes the folder a collection for Jellyfin.
  /media/movies/Heist [boxset]/collection.xml: the collection it belongs to is in a media library, which the export never writes, so the file stays; Jellyfin's metadata refresh may merge the members it lists back into the collection.
  /media/music/Road.xml: the playlist it belongs to is in a media library, which the export never writes, so the file stays; Jellyfin's metadata refresh may merge the members and shares it lists back into the playlist.
  1 playlist or collection in media libraries not found where the export ran (the first: /media/music/Gone [playlist]/playlist.xml): whether each has a metadata file that Jellyfin's metadata refresh may merge back is not known. Export where the media is mounted at the paths Ferrofin used, so each can be checked.

Backups and scheduled tasks:
  2 backup archives in data/backups made by Ferrofin, which Jellyfin cannot restore.
  Scheduled tasks: Ferrofin keeps their triggers in task_triggers.json and their last results in task_results.json, which Jellyfin does not read. Its tasks keep what its own files held before adoption, or its defaults.
